archetype.name: Pocket Passer (timing and rhythm)
archetype.definition: A distributor who wins from a clean pocket on schedule, working the short and intermediate middle to a deep group of targets rather than creating outside the structure.

report.headline: Top-ten efficiency is real, but shootouts and zero interceptions flatter it
report.take:
Goff is in his tenth season as the same quarterback he has been since the Lions rebuilt around him. He throws on time from a clean pocket, distributes to four or five targets, and gets almost nothing from his legs. The 0.289 EPA per dropback ranks 8th and is nearly identical to his 2024 peak (0.293 per play). Through ten seasons his best years have come when the protection and the skill group were both intact, and so far both are. He has been pressured on only 16.1% of dropbacks, 8th lowest, and the ball is going to whoever is open: LaPorta, Jameson Williams and TeSlaa are all near or above half a point of EPA per target.

The production engine is the intermediate game. On 41 throws of 10-19 air yards he is at 0.793 EPA with a 61% success rate, the band where play-action and crossers live. On 88 short throws he completes 76% at 5.8 points over expected. The 11 deep attempts at 1.359 EPA look spectacular, but 11 throws is a sample of a few plays, not a trait. His career aggressiveness and aDOT have always been modest.

The context matters as much as the arm. Detroit's defense ranks 32nd in EPA and dead last against deep passes, so every Lions game has gone over the total and Goff has spent 64 dropbacks trailing by nine or more. Those snaps carry 0.418 EPA against defenses playing soft. In one-score situations he drops to 0.174, which looks a lot like his 2025 season (0.157). The schedule has also been gentle: three of four opponents rank 16th or worse on defense today. Then there are the zero interceptions on 161 attempts. That ranks 1st, but it sits against three turnover-worthy fumbles and a career that has never finished under seven picks in a full season.

Where this goes: the volume is locked in for as long as the defense leaks, and 300-plus-yard weeks will keep coming. Expect the efficiency to settle from top-eight toward the 0.15-0.20 range that has defined his non-peak Detroit years. Interceptions will start to show up. The interior line is the near-term risk, with starting guard Ben Bartch out and center Cade Mays on IR until about Week 7.

strengths.title: Intermediate middle is his kill zone
strengths.body: His throws of 10-19 air yards are producing 0.793 EPA with a 61% success rate, and the middle of the field is his best direction at 0.483 EPA and a 66.7% success rate. That is the signature of a quarterback throwing on rhythm into windows created by scheme and play-action. It is consistent with who he has been in Detroit, so the skill is real, even if 41 attempts will not hold this exact number.

strengths.title: Clean pocket, spread distribution
strengths.body: He has been pressured on only 16.1% of dropbacks, 8th lowest among qualifiers. When the pocket holds he is accurate on short throws, completing 76.1% at 5.8 points over expected. The efficiency is spread around: LaPorta (0.583 EPA per target), TeSlaa (0.511) and Williams (0.496) are all producing, so defenses cannot take away one read.

strengths.title: Red-zone finishing
strengths.body: Eight of his nine touchdowns have come inside the 20, on 34 attempts with 0.426 EPA and accuracy above expected. That reflects a well-designed red-zone menu and quick decisions in tight space. His 5.6% TD rate ranks only 14th, so this is not an outlier that needs to crash.

concerns.title: Zero interceptions won't last
concerns.body: No interceptions on 161 attempts ranks 1st. His history argues against it holding: he threw 8 or more picks in each of the last five seasons and 12 in 2024. He also has three turnover-worthy fumbles with none lost, so the ball-security luck runs both ways. The risk-taking is not new, the results are, and both turnover numbers should move toward his norms.

concerns.title: Efficiency inflated by catch-up script
concerns.body: He has 64 dropbacks while trailing by 9 or more, at 0.418 EPA, against defenses protecting leads. In one-score states he is at 0.174, closer to his 2025 baseline than to his 2024 peak. That gap exists because Detroit's defense ranks 32nd in EPA and gives up more points deep than anyone, which also means the volume will keep coming.

concerns.title: Third downs and a thinned interior line
concerns.body: On third down he is at -0.105 EPA with a 35.9% conversion rate and completions 12.1 points below expected. That is partly the 7.6-yard average distance, and 39 plays is a small sample. The bigger worry is the guard and center spots: Bartch (93% of snaps when healthy) is out and Mays is on IR until about Week 7. Interior pressure is the one thing that breaks a rhythm passer.

trend.note: His EPA per dropback has been positive every week and peaked against Buffalo, while his volume climbed to 52 attempts and 412 yards at Carolina as the defense kept forcing catch-up. The level has held, but against a soft run of defenses.

nextGame.headline: A run-stuffing, pass-leaking defense funnels Detroit to Goff
nextGame.body:
Arizona's defense is built backward for this matchup. It ranks 5th against the run (-0.229 EPA) but 31st against the pass, 31st on short throws, 31st in explosive passes allowed and 30th on deep balls. It also allows 2.75 passing TDs per game to quarterbacks, 30th in the league. With the run game unlikely to find room, Detroit's path is the short and intermediate passing game where Goff lives. Arizona's pass rush is middling: 23rd in hit rate, 12th in sack rate. The one counterweight is that Arizona's offense ranks only 23rd in passing EPA, so the script may not force 50 attempts the way Carolina did.

Availability cuts both ways. Detroit plays without Bartch at guard and without Mays at center, so the interior is the weak point even against an average rush. Arizona lost left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. for the season and guard Isaiah Adams is questionable. Detroit's pass rush ranks 6th in sack rate and that protection was a 100%-snap starter, so the Lions could stall drives and get Goff more possessions. Safety Andrew Wingard (76% of snaps) is questionable with a knee bruise. If he sits, the seams for LaPorta and the deep shots for Williams get easier.

keyMatchups.title: Short-area passing vs. 31st-ranked coverage
keyMatchups.body: Arizona gives up 0.317 EPA on short throws, 31st in the league, which is exactly where Goff throws most (88 attempts, 76% completions). This is not a matchup that needs heroics: quick game and run-after-catch should move the chains.

keyMatchups.title: Run-game dead end forces the pass
keyMatchups.body: Arizona's run defense ranks 5th, and Detroit's rushing offense is only 17th. Expect Detroit to lean further into the pass than its modest +1.2% pass rate over expected suggests.

keyMatchups.title: Lions rush vs. Arizona's reshuffled line
keyMatchups.body: Detroit ranks 6th in sack rate, and Arizona is without its 100%-snap left tackle with a guard questionable. Extra sacks and short drives for Arizona mean more Detroit possessions and a more neutral script for Goff.

nextGame.watch: How Detroit's patched interior holds up early. If Goff is getting clean pockets in the first quarter, Arizona's coverage has no answer for the intermediate middle.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is sustainable for as long as Detroit's defense ranks at the bottom. That points to steady 270-320-yard output and plenty of fourth-quarter passing. What should regress is the efficiency shine: catch-up EPA against soft defenses, the 11-attempt deep sample, and especially the zero interceptions. His career says roughly a pick every other game.

A reasonable expectation is a top-12 efficiency quarterback with top-five volume. The red-zone touchdown rate looks repeatable given his track record, so passing TDs should stay around two a game. The early schedule was soft, so tougher defenses will test whether the one-score-state level (about 0.17 EPA) is the real baseline. Mays' return around Week 7 is the main reinforcement.
swingFactors: Whether Detroit's defense improves and changes the game scripts

bets.reason: All four Lions games have gone over, and combined scores average about 61.5 points. Detroit's defense ranks 32nd in EPA and Arizona's pass defense ranks 31st, so both secondaries leak. Arizona's 23rd-ranked passing offense, now without its left tackle, is the reason this stops short of a strong play.
Arizona allows 2.75 passing TDs per game to quarterbacks (30th). Its 5th-ranked run defense pushes Detroit's red-zone work to the air, where Goff has 8 TDs on 34 attempts.

Arizona ranks 31st in pass EPA and 31st on short throws, which fits his profile. However, it has allowed only 263.5 passing yards a game to quarterbacks, and a more comfortable Detroit lead could trim his attempts from Carolina's 52.

Detroit's offense makes the favorite the natural pick, but the Lions are 0-3-1 against the spread. The 32nd-ranked defense has kept even winning games close: a one-point win over New Orleans as 7-point favorites and a push against the Jets. Laying points with this defense on the road has not paid.

confidence.note: Four games and a soft early schedule, but his profile matches a decade of career data.
